1.title: Timed Mixed Lab Set B
1.text: Welcome to Module eighteen: Timed Mixed Lab Set B. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. How to use this set. Review after the set. Practice with sixteen timed tasks worth one hundred seven points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All five domains (weighted like the exam: Environment, Configuration and Security four tasks, Application Design and Build three, Application Deployment three, Services and Networking three, Observability and Maintenance three). Practice in this module: sixteen tasks, one hundred seven points, about one hundred sixteen minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: How to use this set
1.text: How to use this set. Reset: make sure the lab cluster is healthy ( kube control get nodes shows three Ready nodes). Start a one hundred twenty-minute timer. Allowed documentation only: Kubernetes dot I O or docs and blog, helm dot S H or docs. For each task, prepare its starting state with python run labs dot py the setup flag lab id (it also prints the task), then solve it as you would on the exam. Score yourself with python run labs dot py the check flag lab id. A task is all-or-nothing, like the exam's scoring. Pass mark: sixty-six percent of the points. Exam tip: Do Set A first and Set B a few days later, so you can see whether your routine improved.

1.title: How to use this set, continued
1.text: How to use this set. Honest note: this set reuses tasks from the module labs, so you have seen their wording before. Use it as a timed rehearsal of speed and routine, then use the killer dot S H simulator for tasks you have never seen.

1.title: Review after the set
1.text: Review after the set. Count your points per domain and compare them with the pass mark of sixty-six percent. Write every reading mistake (wrong namespace, wrong name, missing context line) on your personal checklist. Redo the tasks you flagged or failed, this time with the reference solution closed. Compare your domain scores with Set A and redo the three slowest tasks. Exam tip: Compare your domain scores with Set A and redo the three slowest tasks.

1.title: Task 1: Environment
1.text: Task one: Environment. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace sec, create a Secret db creds with username admin and password S three cret exclamation mark. Create a Pod dbclient (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command sleep three thousand six hundred ) that gets the environment variable D B user from the Secret key username and mounts the whole Secret read-only at slash E T C slash db. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 1: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n sec create secret generic db creds the from literal flag set to username admin the from literal flag set to password S three cret exclamation mark. kube control dash n sec apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 1: Solution, continued
1.text: Task one: Solution, continued. Run volume Mounts. Then - name creds, mount Path slash E T C slash db, read Only true. Then volumes. Then - name creds. Then secret secret Name db creds. Then Y. Then kube control dash n sec wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash dbclient the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n sec exec dbclient then the command sh dash c echo D B user cat slash E T C slash db slash password.

1.title: Task 2: Environment
1.text: Task two: Environment. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace res, the Pod of the Deployment hog is repeatedly killed because it uses more memory than its limit ( O O M killed ). Without changing the image or the command, set the memory limit of its container to two hundred fifty-six mebibytes and its memory request to sixty-four mebibytes, and wait until the Deployment has one Ready replica that keeps running. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 2: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n res describe pod dash l app hog then pipe to grep -i E O O M killed then pipe to Reason then pipe to Limits then pipe to memory. Then kube control dash n res set resources deployment hog the requests flag set to memory sixty-four mebibytes the limits flag set to memory two hundred fifty-six mebibytes. Then kube control dash n res rollout status deployment hog the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 3: Environment
1.text: Task three: Environment. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace auth, the Pod caller (Service Account app sa ) asks the A P I server every three seconds for the list of Pods in its own namespace and prints the H T T P status code. It prints four hundred three. Without changing the Pod, give its Service Account exactly the access it needs, namely list on Pods in the namespace auth (use a Role named pod lister and a Role Binding named pod lister binding ), so that the log shows two hundred. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 3: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n auth logs caller then pipe to tail -two. Then kube control dash n auth create role pod lister the verb flag set to list the resource flag set to pods. Then kube control dash n auth create rolebinding pod lister binding the role flag set to pod lister the serviceaccount flag set to auth app sa. Then sleep six. Then kube control dash n auth logs caller then pipe to tail -two. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 4: Environment
1.text: Task four: Environment. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The C R D (Custom Resource Definition) for the kind Widget (group shop dot example dot com ) is installed. The manifest about slash work slash widget dot yaml for the Widget blue one in the namespace crd is rejected by the A P I server. Read the error, fix the manifest without changing the name, and create the object. It must end up with spec dot size three and spec dot color blue. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 4: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control apply dash f about slash work slash widget dot yaml two one then pipe to head -five. Then kube control explain widget dot spec. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control apply dash f about slash work slash widget dot yaml. Then kube control dash n crd get widgets. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 5: Design and Build
1.text: Task five: Design and Build. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace wl, create a Cron Job named tick with the image busy box one dot thirty-six that runs date every five minutes. It must not start a run while the previous one is still running ( concurrency Policy Forbid ), and keep the last two successful and the last one failed Jobs. Then start one run now, by creating a Job named tick manual from the Cron Job, and wait until that Job is complete. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 5: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n wl create cronjob tick the image flag set to busy box one dot thirty-six the schedule flag set to or five then the command date. Then kube control dash n wl patch cronjob tick dash p spec concurrency Policy Forbid, successful Jobs History Limit two, failed Jobs History Limit one. Then kube control dash n wl create job tick manual the from flag set to cronjob slash tick. Then kube control dash n wl wait the for flag set to condition complete job slash tick manual the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 6: Design and Build
2.text: Task six: Design and Build. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context.

2.title: Task 6: Design and Build, continued
2.text: Task six: Design and Build, continued. In the namespace mc, the Job report never completes, because its Pod has a second container tail (a log helper that sleeps forever) next to the main container main. Keep the tail container, but change the Job so that it completes: declare tail as a native sidecar (an init container with restart Policy Always ). The manifest is in about slash work slash report job dot yaml. A Job's Pod template cannot be edited, so delete the Job and create it again from the corrected file; wait until the Job is complete. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 6: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n mc delete job report the wait flag set to true. cat about slash work slash report job dot yaml. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 6: Solution, continued
2.text: Task six: Solution, continued. Run image busy box one dot thirty-six. Then command sleep, three thousand six hundred. Then restart Policy Always. Then containers. Then - name main. Then image busy box one dot thirty-six. Then command sh, dash c, echo report finished. Then Y. Then kube control apply dash f about slash work slash report job dot yaml. The remaining lines are on the screen.

2.title: Task 7: Design and Build
2.text: Task seven: Design and Build. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace vol, create a Persistent Volume Claim named data that requests one gibibyte with Read Write Once from the cluster's default Storage Class (do not name a class). Create a Pod writer (image busy box one dot thirty-six ) that mounts it at slash data and runs sh dash c echo kept after delete slash data slash note dot txt sleep three thousand six hundred. When the file exists, delete the Pod writer and create a Pod reader (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command sleep three thousand six hundred ) that mounts the same claim at slash data. The file must still be there. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 7: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n vol apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 7: Solution, continued
2.text: Task seven: Solution, continued. Run ---. Then api Version version one. Then kind Pod. Then metadata. Then name writer. Then spec. Then containers. Then - name main. Then image busy box one dot thirty-six. The remaining lines are on the screen.

2.title: Task 7: Solution, continued
2.text: Task seven: Solution, continued. Run kube control dash n vol wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash writer the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then sleep three. Then kube control dash n vol delete pod writer the wait flag set to true. kube control dash n vol apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen.

2.title: Task 7: Solution, continued
2.text: Task seven: Solution, continued. Run - name store, mount Path slash data. Then volumes. Then - name store. Then persistent Volume Claim. Then claim Name data. Then Y. Then kube control dash n vol wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash reader the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then kube control dash n vol exec reader then the command cat slash data slash note dot txt.

2.title: Task 8: Deployment
2.text: Task eight: Deployment. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace bg, a blue version (Deployment app blue ) and a green version (Deployment app green ) of an application are both running. The Service shop currently sends all traffic to the blue version. Switch the live traffic to the green version by changing the Service, and leave both Deployments running (so that you can switch back). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 8: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n bg get svc shop dash o json path dot spec dot selector echo. Then kube control dash n bg patch service shop dash p spec selector app shop, version green. Then kube control dash n bg get endpoints shop. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 9: Deployment
2.text: Task nine: Deployment. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The file about slash work slash prod values dot yaml holds the settings for production. Install the newest version of the chart local slash webapp (the repository local is already added) as the release site in the namespace helm ns (create it with the install), taking the values from that file. Do not edit the file. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 9: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run helm show values local slash webapp then pipe to head -twenty. Then helm install site local slash webapp dash n helm ns the create namespace flag dash f about slash work slash prod values dot yaml the wait flag the timeout flag one hundred twenty seconds. Then helm get values site dash n helm ns. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 10: Deployment
2.text: Task ten: Deployment. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. A Kustomize base exists in about slash kust slash base (a Deployment web and a Service web ). Create an overlay in about slash kust slash overlays slash staging that reuses the base and: sets the namespace staging, generates a Config Map named web config with the literal level info, and patches the Deployment so that its container loads all keys of that Config Map as environment variables ( env From ). Do not edit the base. Create the namespace staging and apply the overlay. The running Pod must show level info in its environment. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 10: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. cat about slash kust slash overlays slash staging slash customization dot yaml. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 10: Solution, continued
2.text: Task ten: Solution, continued. Run kube control customize about slash kust slash overlays slash staging then pipe to head -forty. Then kube control create ns staging. Then kube control apply dash k about slash kust slash overlays slash staging. Then kube control dash n staging rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n staging exec deploy slash web then the command printenv level.

2.title: Task 11: Networking
2.text: Task eleven: Networking. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace svc two, expose the Deployment web (engine X on port eighty) with a Service named web np of type Node Port, service port eighty, using the fixed node port thirty thousand eighty. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Task 11: Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc two expose deployment web the name flag set to web np the port flag set to eighty the type flag set to Node Port the dry run flag set, and so on. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control dash n svc two apply dash f slash temp slash web np dot yaml. Then kube control dash n svc two get svc web np. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Task 12: Networking
3.text: Task twelve: Networking. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace ing two, the Service a exists. A certificate and key for secure dot example dot com are in about slash answers slash tls dot crt and about slash answers slash tls dot key. Create a T L S Secret named web tls from them, and an Ingress named secure (class traefik ) that serves the host secure dot example dot com from the Service a on port eighty and uses the Secret for H T T P S. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Task 12: Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n ing two create secret tls web tls the cert flag set to H O M E slash answers slash tls dot crt the key flag set to H O M, and so on. Then kube control dash n ing two create ingress secure the class flag set to traefik the rule flag set to secure dot example dot com or a eighty,tls web tls. Then kube control dash n ing two get ingress secure. Then sleep five. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Task 13: Networking
3.text: Task thirteen: Networking. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace np three, the Pod app (busy box) must only be allowed to send traffic to (a) Pods labelled app db on T C P port eighty and (b) the cluster D N S on port fifty-three (U D P and T C P). All other outgoing traffic from app must be blocked. Create one Network Policy named app egress for the Pod app. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Task 13: Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n np three apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then sleep five. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Task 14: Observability
3.text: Task fourteen: Observability. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The Pod slow in the namespace probes (manifest about slash work slash slow dot yaml ) needs about twenty-five seconds to start, but its liveness probe starts checking after one second and keeps killing it. Without removing or loosening the liveness probe, add a startup probe to the container that runs the same command test dash f slash temp slash started every five seconds with failure Threshold twelve, so that the liveness probe only begins after the app has started. Recreate the Pod from the corrected manifest. It must become Ready with restart Count zero. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Task 14: Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n probes delete pod slow the wait flag set to true. cat about slash work slash slow dot yaml. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Task 14: Solution, continued
3.text: Task fourteen: Solution, continued. Run command sh, dash c, test dash f slash temp slash started. Then period Seconds five. Then failure Threshold twelve. Then liveness Probe. Then exec. Then command sh, dash c, test dash f slash temp slash started. Then initial Delay Seconds one. Then period Seconds two. Then failure Threshold two. The remaining lines are on the screen.

3.title: Task 15: Observability
3.text: Task fifteen: Observability. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace dbg, the Pod of the Deployment svc does not start ( create container config error ). Find the cause with kube control describe, and fix it without changing the Deployment: create what is missing so that the Deployment has one Ready replica. The application expects level info from that source. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Task 15: Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n dbg describe pod dash l app svc then pipe to grep dash i -A three Events. Then kube control dash n dbg create configmap app config the from literal flag set to level info. Then kube control dash n dbg rollout status deployment svc the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Task 16: Observability
3.text: Task sixteen: Observability. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The Pod shop in the namespace dbg has two containers, web and worker. Write only the last three lines of the log of the container worker to about slash answers slash worker tail dot txt on the host where you run kube control. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Task 16: Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n dbg logs shop dash c worker the tail flag set to three about slash answers slash worker tail dot txt. Then cat about slash answers slash worker tail dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Recall Check 1
3.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many points do you need to pass the set, and what is the passing score of the exam? Answer: sixty-six percent of the points, the same as the exam. Question two. What is the first action on every task? Answer: Run the context line and note the exact names and namespaces. Question three. What do you do with a task that is stuck after about six minutes? Answer: Flag it, move on and return at the end.

3.title: Recall Check 2
3.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which command shows why a Pod is Pending or crashing? Answer: kube control describe pod, then kube control logs ( the previous flag after a restart). Question five. Which two flags generate yamel without creating the object? Answer: the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml. Question six. How do you confirm that a Service has working backends? Answer: kube control get endpoints service and a test request from a throw-away Pod.

3.title: Module Recap
3.text: Here is the recap. Time: one hundred twenty minutes, about six to eight minutes per task. Pass: sixty-six percent of the points; tasks are all-or-nothing. Order: easy first, flag the hard ones, keep time to verify. Verify: a second command ( get, describe, logs, a test request). After the set: repeat the tasks you flagged, then the other set. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. In the next module, we continue the course.
